s: Where is the headquarters of the Eastern Naval Command, India's largest naval command?
x: The Eastern Naval Command is headquartered at Visakhapatnam, facing the Bay of Bengal, and is India's largest naval command.

s: With which country did India begin the Malabar naval exercise in 1992 as a bilateral exercise?
x: Malabar began as an India-US exercise in 1992; Japan became permanent in 2015 and Australia joined in 2020.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about India's naval exercises and maritime platforms?
o: MILAN is a bilateral exercise of the Indian Navy
AIKEYME stands for Africa-India Key Maritime Engagement
The 2022 and 2024 editions of MILAN were held at Visakhapatnam
The first AIKEYME was held at Dar es Salaam, Tanzania, in 2025
x: MILAN is a multilateral exercise hosted by the Indian Navy, not a bilateral one.

s: In which country was the first AIKEYME exercise with African navies held in 2025?
x: AIKEYME, India's exercise with African navies, was first held in 2025 in Tanzania.

s: On board which ship did the IOS SAGAR mission of 2026 sail from Mumbai?
x: IOS SAGAR sailed on INS Sunayna; INS Sumedha carried the President at the 2026 Fleet Review.

s: In which year did Australia join the Malabar naval exercise, making it a Quad exercise?
x: Malabar began as India-US in 1992; Japan became permanent in 2015 and Australia joined in 2020.

s: What kind of exercise is MILAN, the Indian Navy exercise first held at Port Blair in 1995?
o: Trilateral exercise with Japan and the USA
x: MILAN is a multilateral Indian Navy exercise, first held at Port Blair in 1995, not a bilateral one.

s: In which year did Japan become a permanent partner in the Malabar naval exercise?
x: Malabar began as India-US in 1992; Japan became permanent in 2015 and Australia joined in 2020.

s: Aboard which ship did President Murmu review the fleet at the International Fleet Review 2026 at Visakhapatnam?
x: The President reviewed the 2026 IFR aboard INS Sumedha; INS Sunayna carried IOS SAGAR.

s: Before 2026, in which year did Visakhapatnam last host the International Fleet Review?
x: Visakhapatnam hosted the IFR in 2016 and again in 2026.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about SAGAR (Security and Growth for All in the Region)?
o: It widened India's maritime vision to the Indo-Pacific and the Global South
It aims to make India the net security provider in the Indian Ocean Region
It is seen as countering China's 'String of Pearls'
x: Widening the vision to the Indo-Pacific and the Global South is MAHASAGAR (2025), not SAGAR.

s: In which year was MAHASAGAR, which widens SAGAR to the Indo-Pacific and the Global South, introduced?
x: MAHASAGAR was introduced in 2025, extending SAGAR (2015) to the Indo-Pacific and the Global South.

s: In which year was the Indian Ocean Naval Symposium (IONS) launched by the Indian Navy, with its first meeting in New Delhi?
x: IONS was launched in 2008; the claim of an inaugural IONS in 2015 is a known trap.

s: Where was the 9th Conclave of Chiefs of the Indian Ocean Naval Symposium hosted?
x: India hosted the 9th IONS Conclave of Chiefs at Visakhapatnam.

s: Where is the Information Fusion Centre – Indian Ocean Region (IFC-IOR), set up in December 2018, located?
x: IFC-IOR is at Gurugram, not Visakhapatnam; it serves maritime domain awareness and information sharing.

s: In which year was the IMO-backed Djibouti Code of Conduct against piracy adopted?
x: The Djibouti Code of Conduct was adopted in 2009; India joined it as an observer in 2020.

s: India took command for the first time of which maritime task force in 2026?
o: Indian Ocean Naval Symposium Task Force
x: India took command for the first time of CTF-154, a task force of the Combined Maritime Forces headquartered in Bahrain.

s: SHANTI is India's security framework for which region?
x: SHANTI is India's Bay of Bengal security framework, alongside SAGAR and MAHASAGAR.

s: Where was the 9th Indian Ocean Conference, organised by the India Foundation, held?
x: The Indian Ocean Conference, held since 2016 by the India Foundation, had its 9th edition in Mauritius.

s: What is the full form of MAHASAGAR, India's maritime vision of 2025?
o: Maritime Hub for Advancement of Security and Growth Across Regions
Mutual and Holistic Advancement for Security Across the Regions
Maritime Alliance for Holistic Security and Growth in All Regions
Mutual Help for Asian Security and Growth Across Regions
x: MAHASAGAR (2025) means Mutual and Holistic Advancement for Security Across the Regions; it widens SAGAR.

s: In which year did India become an observer to the Djibouti Code of Conduct against piracy?
x: The IMO-backed Djibouti Code was adopted on 29 January 2009; India became an observer in 2020.

s: The IFC-IOR at Gurugram is collocated with which of the following?
o: Indian National Centre for Ocean Information Services
x: The IFC-IOR (Dec 2018) is collocated with IMAC at Gurugram for maritime domain awareness.

s: How many member navies does the Indian Ocean Naval Symposium (IONS) have?
x: IONS has 25 members and 9 observers (34 navies in all) after South Korea joined as an observer in 2023.

s: Which countries are involved in the newer trilateral initiative for a Persian Gulf–Black Sea corridor?
x: The newer initiative involves Armenia, Iran and India and promotes a Persian Gulf–Black Sea corridor.

s: Chabahar port is located in which part of Iran?
o: Fars on the Gulf of Oman
Sistan-Baluchestan on the Gulf of Oman
x: Chabahar is located in Iran’s Sistan-Baluchestan province on the Gulf of Oman.

s: When was the IMEC announced at the G20 New Delhi Summit?
x: The India-Middle East-Europe Corridor was announced at the G20 New Delhi Summit in September 2023.

s: Which of the following pairs relating to the INSTC is correctly matched?
o: Original signatories – India, Iran and Russia
Route from Mumbai – Via Afghanistan to Central Asia
x: The 2000 INSTC agreement was signed by India, Iran and Russia; the route runs from Mumbai via Iran, and the western branch passes through Azerbaijan.

s: The Kaladan project links Kolkata to Mizoram through which Myanmar port?
x: The Kaladan route runs Kolkata – Sittwe – Paletwa – Mizoram.

s: In which year did India join the Ashgabat Agreement, signed in 2011?
x: The Ashgabat Agreement dates from 2011; India joined it in 2018.

s: Through which country does the western branch of the International North-South Transport Corridor pass?
x: The INSTC (2000; India, Iran, Russia) has a western branch through Azerbaijan.

s: Which of the following is NOT a partner of the India-Middle East-Europe Economic Corridor (IMEC)?
x: IMEC partners are India, UAE, Saudi Arabia, EU, France, Germany, Italy and USA; Iran is not one.

s: The Ashgabat Agreement (2011) seeks a transport corridor between Central Asia and which region?
x: The Ashgabat Agreement (2011) links Central Asia with the Persian Gulf; India joined it in 2018.

s: In which year was the International North-South Transport Corridor (INSTC) agreement signed by India, Iran and Russia?
x: The INSTC was launched in 2000 by India, Iran and Russia, linking Mumbai to St. Petersburg via Iran and the Caspian.

s: Through which company does India develop the Shahid Beheshti terminal at Chabahar port?
x: India develops the Shahid Beheshti terminal through India Ports Global Ltd (IPGL).

s: For how many years is India's operating contract for Chabahar's Shahid Beheshti terminal, signed in May 2024?
x: The May 2024 contract is for 10 years, not 20.

s:
Consider the following statements about Chabahar port:
1. It lies in Sistan-Baluchestan on the Gulf of Oman.
2. It gives India access to Afghanistan and Central Asia bypassing Pakistan.
3. Its terminal was damaged in the US strikes of July 2026.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct; statement 3 is wrong because the terminal was not damaged in the July 2026 US strikes.

s: Visakhapatnam holds one of India’s three:
x: Visakhapatnam holds one of India’s three Strategic Petroleum Reserves.

s: TAPI and IPI pipelines are respectively associated with which countries?
x: TAPI stands for Turkmenistan-Afghanistan-Pakistan-India, while IPI stands for Iran-Pakistan-India and is also called the Peace Pipeline.

s: India imports about what share of its crude oil needs?
x: India imports about 88% of its crude oil needs; about 50% is the share of natural gas imported.

s: Which of the following is NOT one of the four ‘A’s guiding India’s energy policy?
x: The four ‘A’s are availability, accessibility, affordability and acceptability. Autonomy is not included in the stated formulation.

s: India's Strategic Petroleum Reserves are at Visakhapatnam, Mangaluru and which other place?
x: India's SPRs are at Visakhapatnam, Mangaluru and Padur, with 5.33 MMT capacity.

s: India's Strategic Petroleum Reserves cover about how many days of demand?
x: India's SPR covers about 9.5 days, against the IEA norm of 90 days.

s: Which country is the only one storing crude oil in India's Strategic Petroleum Reserve?
x: The UAE, India's 4th crude supplier, is the only country storing oil in India's SPR.

s: Which pipeline project is popularly called the 'Peace Pipeline'?
x: The Iran-Pakistan-India (IPI) gas pipeline, about 2,775 km, is called the 'Peace Pipeline'.

s: What is India's rank among the world's energy consumers?
x: India is the third-largest energy consumer in the world, not the second.

s: What is the total capacity of India's Strategic Petroleum Reserves at Visakhapatnam, Mangaluru and Padur?
x: The three SPRs hold 5.33 MMT of crude, about 9.5 days of demand.

s: What is India's status in the International Energy Agency?
x: India has been an Association country of the IEA since 2017 and is not a full member.

s: Where is the headquarters of the treaty-based International Solar Alliance (ISA) located?
x: The ISA is treaty-based with its headquarters at Gurugram. Paris (COP21) is where it was launched, not its HQ; New Delhi is a distractor; Riyadh hosts the IEF secretariat.

s: Where was the International Solar Alliance (ISA) launched on 30 November 2015?
o: The G20 Summit in New Delhi
x: The ISA was launched on 30 November 2015 at COP21 in Paris.

s: Where was the Global Biofuels Alliance launched in 2023?
o: The World Energy Congress in Abu Dhabi
The BRICS Summit in South Africa
x: The Global Biofuels Alliance was launched in 2023 at the G20 Summit in India.

s:
Consider the following statements about the International Energy Forum (IEF):
1. Its secretariat is located at Riyadh.
2. India hosted the 16th IEF ministerial meeting in 2023.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statement 1 is correct: the IEF secretariat is at Riyadh. Statement 2 is wrong: India hosted the 16th IEF ministerial in 2018, not 2023. So 1 only (A); B, C and D accept the wrong year or reject statement 1.

s: With which body is the 'One Sun One World One Grid' initiative associated?
x: One Sun One World One Grid is linked with the International Solar Alliance, headquartered at Gurugram.

s: Which one of the following sets is associated with the concept of China’s ‘String of Pearls’?
x: Gwadar, Hambantota and Djibouti are associated with the String of Pearls concept.

s: Which of the following ports are India’s counters to China’s Belt and Road Initiative?
x: Chabahar, Sittwe and Sabang are identified as India’s counters to China’s BRI.

s: In strategic analysis, China's port-building strategy in the Indian Ocean is linked to which of the following?
x: China’s port-building is linked to its perceived Malacca dilemma.

s: Which one of the following port-country pairs is NOT correctly matched?
x: Sittwe is in Myanmar, not Sri Lanka. Sabang is in Indonesia, Duqm in Oman and Agalega in Mauritius.

s: In which country is Duqm, a port giving India strategic access, located?
x: Duqm is in Oman; Sabang is in Indonesia, Agalega in Mauritius and Sittwe in Myanmar.

s: Where was China's first overseas military base set up in 2017?
x: Djibouti hosts China's first overseas base (2017) and the US Camp Lemonnier.

s: Diego Garcia in the Indian Ocean hosts a military base of which country or countries?
x: Diego Garcia is a US-UK base; a UK-Mauritius treaty on it was signed in May 2025.

s: Agalega, where India has built an airstrip and a jetty, belongs to which country?
x: Agalega is an island of Mauritius where India has built an airstrip and a jetty.

s: Diego Garcia, a US-UK military base, was the subject of a treaty in May 2025 between the UK and which country?
x: In May 2025 the UK and Mauritius signed a treaty on Diego Garcia (Chagos Islands).

s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Continental shelf — exactly 200 nautical miles in every case
x: The EEZ extends up to 200 nautical miles. The contiguous zone extends to 24 nautical miles, the territorial sea to 12 nautical miles, and the continental shelf may extend up to 350 nautical miles.

s: Samudrayaan, concerned with deep-sea mining and the study of polymetallic nodules, is a component of which programme?
x: Samudrayaan is part of India's Deep Ocean Mission and concerns deep-sea mining and polymetallic nodules.

s: In which year was the India-Bangladesh maritime boundary dispute settled by an award of the Permanent Court of Arbitration?
x: The PCA award of 2014 settled the India-Bangladesh maritime boundary, giving Bangladesh about 19,467 sq km of the 25,602 sq km disputed area. 2009, 2012 and 2015 are not the year of this award.

s: Of the 25,602 sq km disputed area, how much did the 2014 PCA award give Bangladesh?
x: The 2014 PCA award gave Bangladesh 19,467 of the 25,602 sq km.

s: Matsya-6000 is part of which of the following?
x: Matsya-6000 and Samudrayaan are under the Deep Ocean Mission.

s: Under UNCLOS, up to what distance does the Exclusive Economic Zone extend?
x: The EEZ extends to 200 nm; 12 nm is the territorial sea, 24 nm the contiguous zone and 350 nm the outer shelf limit.

s: What is the length of India's coastline according to the latest estimate?
x: India's coastline is now measured at 11,098.81 km (earlier 7,516.6 km).

s: Under UNCLOS, up to what distance from the baseline does the territorial sea extend?
x: The territorial sea is 12 nm, contiguous zone 24 nm, EEZ 200 nm, and the shelf up to 350 nm.

s: Following which major event was the National Investigation Agency Act enacted in 2008?
x: The NIA Act was enacted in 2008 after the 26/11 Mumbai attacks.

s: The Intelligence Bureau was set up in which year?
x: The Intelligence Bureau was set up in 1887.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct?
o: The NIA is a voluntary auxiliary force raised by the States
The NIA functions under the Ministry of Home Affairs
The NIA can investigate scheduled offences anywhere in India without State consent
Home Guards are voluntary auxiliary forces under the States
x: Home Guards, not the NIA, are voluntary auxiliary forces of the States; the NIA is a central agency under the MHA.

s: Which force protects the Prime Minister and former Prime Ministers?
x: The SPG (SPG Act 1988) protects the PM and former PMs; the NSG ('Black Cats') is the MHA counter-terror force.

s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Home Guards — voluntary auxiliary force under the States
CERT-In — Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology
Internal Security Academy — CRPF, Mount Abu
x: NATGRID is an intelligence grid under the Ministry of Home Affairs, not the Ministry of External Affairs. The other three pairs are correctly matched.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Research and Analysis Wing – Internal intelligence under the MHA
Research and Analysis Wing – External intelligence
Intelligence Bureau – External intelligence under the Cabinet Secretariat
x: RAW (1968) is India's external intelligence agency under the Cabinet Secretariat; the IB (1887) handles internal intelligence under the MHA.

s: Under which of the following does CERT-In function?
x: CERT-In is under MeitY; RAW is under the Cabinet Secretariat and IB under the MHA.

s: What are commandos of the National Security Guard (NSG) popularly called?
x: NSG, under the MHA, is known as the 'Black Cats'; Greyhounds and C-60 are State anti-Naxal forces.

s: Under which of the following does NATGRID function?
x: NATGRID is under the MHA, not the MEA.

s: In which year was the Research and Analysis Wing (RAW) set up?
x: RAW, India's external intelligence agency under the Cabinet Secretariat, was set up on 21 September 1968 under Indira Gandhi.

s: In which year was the Special Protection Group Act enacted?
x: The SPG was formed in 1985 and the SPG Act came in 1988; it protects the PM and former PMs.

s: Who headed the Intelligence Bureau in June 2026?
x: Mahesh Dixit, an AP cadre officer, was head of the IB (under the MHA) in June 2026.

s: The ITBP guards the high-altitude China border from the Karakoram Pass to which place?
x: The ITBP, raised in 1962, guards the China border from Karakoram Pass to Jachep La, with posts at 9,000–18,800 feet.

s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
x: Assam Rifles guards the Myanmar border. The BSF, ITBP and SSB are correctly matched with their principal border responsibilities.

s: The Coast Guard is responsible for coastal security in territorial waters and functions under which Ministry?
x: The Coast Guard provides coastal security in territorial waters and functions under the Ministry of Defence.

s: In Punjab and West Bengal, the BSF's jurisdiction inside the international border was extended from 15 km to what distance?
x: BSF jurisdiction in Punjab and West Bengal was extended from 15 km to 50 km; States objected as Police and Public Order are in the State List.

s: The Comprehensive Integrated Border Management System (CIBMS), a technology-based smart-fencing system, is meant mainly for India's borders with which countries?
x: CIBMS is a technology-based smart-fencing system for the Pakistan and Bangladesh borders.

s: Which is India's oldest paramilitary force?
x: Assam Rifles (1835) is the oldest; the CRPF began in 1939 as the Crown Representative's Police.

s: Which is India's newest border guarding force?
x: The SSB, guarding Nepal (2001) and Bhutan (2004), is the newest border force; Assam Rifles is the oldest.

s: Under what name did the CRPF begin on 27 July 1939?
x: The CRPF began on 27 July 1939 as the Crown Representative's Police.

s: Which border guarding force was raised in 1835?
x: Assam Rifles was raised in 1835; the BSF dates from 1965, the ITBP from 1962 and the SSB from 1963.

s: India's border with which country is guarded by the Assam Rifles?
x: Assam Rifles guards the Myanmar border, not Bangladesh, which is with the BSF.

s: In which year was the Department of Border Management created?
x: The Department of Border Management was created in 2004 in the Ministry of Home Affairs.

s: In which year was the Indo-Tibetan Border Police (ITBP) raised?
x: The ITBP was raised in 1962 after the Chinese aggression; it guards the 3,488 km China border.

s: In which year was the Indian Coast Guard set up?
x: The Coast Guard was set up in 1977; it guards territorial waters under the Ministry of Defence.

s: In which year was the Sashastra Seema Bal (SSB), first known as the Special Service Bureau, raised?
x: The SSB was raised in 1963 as the Special Service Bureau; it now guards the Nepal and Bhutan borders.

s: Withdrawal of general consent for the CBI and the wider reach of the NIA and BSF are criticised as intruding into which State subjects?
x: The criticism is that these moves enter the State subjects of police and public order.

s: India shares its longest international land border with:
x: The Bangladesh border (4,096.7 km) is longer than the China (3,488 km), Pakistan (3,323 km) and Nepal (1,751 km) borders.

s: What is the period of the Vibrant Villages Programme-II (VVP-II)?
x: VVP-II runs from 2024-25 to 2028-29 and covers villages on the Pakistan, Bangladesh, Myanmar, Nepal and Bhutan borders.

s: In the three-tier coastal-security arrangement after 26/11, who is responsible for shallow waters?
x: Coastal police cover shallow waters, the Coast Guard territorial waters, and the Navy has overall responsibility.

s: India shares its shortest international land border with:
x: The Afghanistan border (106 km) is the shortest; Bangladesh (4,096.7 km) is the longest.

s: Phase I of the Vibrant Villages Programme covers villages on India's border with which country?
x: Phase I covers China-border states; VVP-II covers the Pakistan, Bangladesh, Myanmar, Nepal and Bhutan borders.

s: What is Sagar Kavach?
x: Sagar Kavach is a biannual coastal-security exercise.

s: How many marine police stations were sanctioned for Andhra Pradesh in Phase I (2005) of the Coastal Security Scheme?
x: Six marine police stations were sanctioned for AP in Phase I (2005); 15 had been sanctioned by 2022.

s: What is the length of India's border with China?
x: India's border with China is 3,488 km; Bangladesh (4,096.7 km) is the longest and Pakistan is 3,323 km.

s: PM-DevINE is a development scheme for which region?
x: PM-DevINE (Prime Minister's Development Initiative for North East) is for the North East.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Chief of Defence Staff (CDS)?
o: The CDS heads the Department of Military Affairs
The CDS is military adviser to the Nuclear Command Authority
The CDS is Permanent Chairman of the Chiefs of Staff Committee
The CDS is the principal military adviser to the Prime Minister
x: The CDS is principal military adviser to the Defence Minister, not the Prime Minister.

s: Who became India's first Chief of Defence Staff on 1 January 2020?
x: Gen Bipin Rawat became the first CDS on 1 January 2020, after the post was created in December 2019. Naravane, Dalbir Singh and V.K. Singh were Army Chiefs but not the first CDS.

s: What is the maximum age for the Chief of Defence Staff?
x: The CDS can serve up to a maximum age of 65.

s: Which department of the Ministry of Defence is headed by the Chief of Defence Staff?
x: The CDS heads the Department of Military Affairs in the MoD.

s: Who chairs the Defence Acquisition Council?
x: The Defence Minister, not the CDS, chairs the Defence Acquisition Council.

s: Who is the present Chief of Defence Staff of India?
x: Gen Anil Chauhan is the present CDS; Gen Bipin Rawat was the first (1 January 2020).

s: When was the post of Chief of Defence Staff (CDS) created?
x: The CDS post was created in December 2019; Gen Bipin Rawat took over as first CDS on 1 January 2020.

s: What were the responses associated with the Uri and Pulwama attacks respectively?
o: Operation Cactus and Operation Blue Star
x: The Uri attack in 2016 was followed by surgical strikes, while the Pulwama attack in 2019 was followed by Balakot action.

s: In which State is the insurgent group United Liberation Front of Asom (ULFA) based?
x: ULFA is based in Assam; NSCN is based in Nagaland and the People's War Group in Andhra Pradesh.

s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: ULFA — Paresh Baruah and Arabinda Rajkhowa
NSCN — Isak Chishi Swu, Th. Muivah and S.S. Khaplang
x: Lashkar-e-Taiba is associated with Hafiz Saeed. Masood Azhar is associated with Jaish-e-Mohammed.

s: Who founded Jaish-e-Mohammed?
x: Masood Azhar founded Jaish-e-Mohammed; Hafiz Saeed (with Zafar Iqbal) founded Lashkar-e-Taiba.

s: The Resistance Front (TRF) is a proxy of which group?
x: TRF is a proxy of Lashkar-e-Taiba.

s: Who, along with Isak Chishi Swu and Th. Muivah, founded NSCN in 1980?
x: NSCN was founded by Isak Chishi Swu, Th. Muivah and S.S. Khaplang; Baruah and Rajkhowa are ULFA leaders.

s: In which year was the United Liberation Front of Asom (ULFA) formed?
x: ULFA was formed in Assam in 1979 by leaders including Paresh Baruah and Arabinda Rajkhowa.

s: In which year was Lashkar-e-Taiba founded by Hafiz Saeed in Kunar, Afghanistan?
x: Lashkar-e-Taiba was founded in 1990 at Kunar, Afghanistan, by Hafiz Saeed; TRF is its proxy.

s: Which agency filed a chargesheet against Hafiz Saeed?
x: The National Investigation Agency filed the chargesheet against Hafiz Saeed.

s: In which year was the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act enacted?
x: UAPA was enacted in 1967 and amended in 2004, 2008, 2012 and 2019.

s: In which year did TADA, enacted in 1985, lapse?
x: TADA was enacted in 1985 and lapsed in 1995.

s: Which section of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, which replaced the IPC from 1 July 2024, defines a terrorist act?
x: The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita replaced the IPC from 1 July 2024, and its Section 113 defines a terrorist act.

s: In which year did the Coimbatore blasts take place?
x: The Coimbatore blasts were in 1998, after the Rajiv Gandhi assassination (1991) and Mumbai blasts (1993) and before the Parliament attack (2001).

s: Which matters does the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act, 1967 primarily address as a national security framework?
o: Disruptive activities, unlawful associations and terror funding
Paper leaks and organized cheating in central competitive exams
Religious character of places of worship on August 15, 1947
Conditions of marriage, divorce and restitution of conjugal rights
x: UAPA, 1967, is a national-security law against disruptive activities, unlawful associations and terror funding. Paper leaks are covered by the 2024 Public Examinations Act.

s: India has kept the Indus Waters Treaty in abeyance since 23 April 2025 until Pakistan:
o: Agrees to a neutral expert under the World Bank
x: The Indus Waters Treaty has been in abeyance since 23 April 2025 (after Pahalgam) until Pakistan ends cross-border terrorism. The other conditions (neutral expert, PoK, GCTF) are not the stated condition.

s: On which date did the terrorist attack on India's Parliament take place?
x: The Parliament attack was on 13 December 2001.

s: In which year was POTA, enacted in 2002, repealed?
x: POTA was enacted in 2002 and repealed in 2004; 2008 is the year of the NIA Act.

s: What did the 2019 amendment to the UAPA allow?
o: Individuals to be designated as terrorists
x: The 2019 UAPA amendment allows individuals to be designated as terrorists.

s: When did the MHA release India's first National Counter-Terrorism Policy?
x: The MHA released India's first National Counter-Terrorism Policy in December 2025.

s: In which year was the Armed Forces (Special Powers) Act (AFSPA) enacted?
x: AFSPA was enacted in 1958; UAPA came in 1967 and TADA in 1985.

s: Where was Rajiv Gandhi assassinated by the LTTE on 21 May 1991?
x: Rajiv Gandhi was assassinated by the LTTE at Sriperumbudur on 21 May 1991.

s: Which law of 2024, in force from 21 June 2024, deals with paper leaks in public examinations?
o: Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Act
x: The Public Examinations Act of 2024 (in force 21 June 2024) targets paper leaks.

s: Near which place did Operation Mahadev (2025), in which the Army and J&K Police killed the Pahalgam attack mastermind and two LeT terrorists, take place?
x: Operation Mahadev (APPSC 2025) was in J&K near Dachigam National Park. Gadchiroli is the C-60 anti-Naxal theatre, Amritsar was Operation Blue Star (1984) and Sriperumbudur was the site of Rajiv Gandhi's assassination (1991).

s: What was Operation Sindoor, which began on 7 May 2025?
o: Army civic-action work in Jammu and Kashmir
Strikes on terror infrastructure in Pakistan after the Pahalgam attack
A 1988 operation to reverse a coup in the Maldives
A tri-service drill on the western border in Gujarat and Rajasthan
x: Operation Sindoor struck terror infrastructure in Pakistan from 7 May 2025, after the Pahalgam attack of 22 April 2025. Civic action in J&K is Sadbhavana, the Maldives coup reversal is Cactus (1988), and the western-border drill is Trishul 2025.

s: Operation Blue Star of 1984 was associated with which place and objective?
o: Golden Temple, Amritsar and flushing out militants
x: Operation Blue Star was conducted in 1984 at the Golden Temple in Amritsar to flush out militants.

s: In which country did India intervene under Operation Cactus (1988)?
x: Operation Cactus (1988) reversed a coup in the Maldives.

s: Where do the C-60 anti-Naxal commandos operate?
x: The C-60 commandos are Gadchiroli's (Maharashtra) anti-Naxal force.

s: What was Trishul 2025?
o: Tri-service drill on the western border
Operation to kill the Pahalgam mastermind
x: Trishul 2025 was a tri-service drill along the western border (Gujarat, Rajasthan).

s: Which of the following pairs relating to the People's War Group is correctly matched?
x: PWG was founded in 1980 by Kondapalli Seetharamaiah, was based in Andhra Pradesh and merged into the CPI (Maoist) in 2004.

s: The ethnic conflict in Manipur has primarily been between which communities, beginning in May 2023?
x: The conflict in Manipur has primarily been between the Meitei and Kuki communities since May 2023.

s: In which year was the Greyhounds force of Andhra Pradesh raised?
x: The Greyhounds, Andhra Pradesh’s special anti-Naxal force, were raised in 1989.

s: “Legacy Thrust Territories” is a concept of the Ministry of Home Affairs intended to:
o: Develop areas cleared of Left Wing Extremism so that it does not revive
x: The concept focuses on developing areas cleared of LWE to prevent the resurgence of extremism.

s: Where is the base of Andhra Pradesh's Greyhounds force?
x: The Greyhounds, raised in 1989, are based at Anandapuram (Visakhapatnam).

s:
Consider the following statements about the Greyhounds:
1. It is Andhra Pradesh's force against left-wing extremism.
2. It cut Naxal activity in Alluri Sitharama Raju and Parvathipuram Manyam districts.
3. It broke red corridors on the Andhra-Odisha Border.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: All three are correct: the Greyhounds fight left-wing extremism, cut Naxal activity in those districts and broke red corridors on the AOB.

s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Golden Crescent - Afghanistan, Iran and Pakistan
2. Golden Triangle - Myanmar, Laos and Bangladesh
Which of the pairs given above is/are correctly matched?
x: Pair 1 is correct: the Golden Crescent is Afghanistan, Iran and Pakistan. Pair 2 is wrong: the Golden Triangle is Myanmar, Laos and Thailand, not Bangladesh. So 1 only (A); B, C and D accept pair 2 or reject pair 1.

s: The Golden Triangle of drug production comprises Myanmar, Laos and which other country?
x: The Golden Triangle is Myanmar, Laos and Thailand, not Bangladesh.

s: In terror financing, what does FICN refer to?
x: FICN is fake Indian currency, used alongside hawala and narcotics for terror financing.

s: With which of the following is PM-Vidyalaxmi associated?
o: Upgrading primary schools in educationally backward areas
Foundational literacy and numeracy by Grade 3
Collateral-free and guarantor-free loans for students admitted to top-quality HEIs
x: PM-Vidyalaxmi provides collateral-free and guarantor-free loans to students admitted to top-quality higher educational institutions.

s: What was the aim of Operation Blackboard (1987), launched under the National Policy on Education 1986?
o: Free online courses for secondary students
x: Operation Blackboard provided minimum facilities in primary schools, especially in educationally backward areas.

s: Which programme provides free massive open online courses from Class 9 to the postgraduate level?
x: SWAYAM provides free MOOCs from Class 9 to the postgraduate level.

s: Which levels of school education does Samagra Shiksha (2018) cover?
x: Samagra Shiksha covers pre-school to Class 12; NIPUN Bharat targets foundational literacy and numeracy by Grade 3.

s: By which grade does NIPUN Bharat (2021) aim to achieve foundational literacy and numeracy?
x: NIPUN Bharat targets foundational literacy and numeracy by Grade 3.

s: For whom is DIKSHA, launched in 2017, mainly meant?
x: DIKSHA is the teachers' platform; SWAYAM offers MOOCs to students and Vidyanjali links schools with volunteers.

s: With whom does the Vidyanjali (2021) portal link government and aided schools?
x: Vidyanjali is the school volunteer portal linking schools with volunteers, NGOs and CSR donors.

s: PM SHRI aims to upgrade over 14,500 schools to showcase which policy?
x: PM SHRI (Cabinet 7 Sep 2022) upgrades 14,500+ schools as showcases of NEP 2020.

s: Samagra Shiksha (2018) merged SSA, RMSA and which other scheme?
x: Samagra Shiksha merged SSA, RMSA and Teacher Education.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct?
o: SWAYAM offers MOOCs from Class 9 to postgraduate level
DIKSHA is a platform mainly for teachers
Operation Blackboard was launched under NPE 1986
NIPUN Bharat targets literacy and numeracy by Grade 5
x: NIPUN Bharat targets foundational literacy and numeracy by Grade 3, not Grade 5.

s: Which of the following is NOT a parameter of the National Institutional Ranking Framework (NIRF)?
x: NIRF uses Teaching-Learning, Research and Professional Practice, Graduation Outcomes, Outreach-Inclusivity and Perception; foreign faculty ratio is not a parameter.

s: What was the main aim of Saakshar Bharat, launched on 8 September 2009?
o: Free online courses for college students
x: Saakshar Bharat aimed at adult literacy, especially of women, in districts with female literacy below 50%.

s: In which year were the Regional Engineering Colleges renamed National Institutes of Technology?
x: RECs were renamed NITs in 2002 and became Institutes of National Importance from 2007.

s: Saakshar Bharat (2009) focused on districts with female literacy below what level?
x: Saakshar Bharat aimed at adult literacy, especially of women, in districts with female literacy below 50%.

s: Up to which year has PMAY-Gramin been extended?
x: PMAY-G has been extended to 2028-29, with 2 crore more houses for 2024-25 to 2028-29.

s: PMAY-G was restructured from which earlier rural housing programme?
o: Basic Services to the Urban Poor
x: Pradhan Mantri Awaas Yojana-Gramin was restructured from Indira Awaas Yojana. IAY began in 1985 and became independent in 1996.

s: What is the unit assistance for a house in hilly areas under PMAY-Gramin?
x: PMAY-G gives Rs 1.30 lakh in hilly areas and Rs 1.20 lakh in plains, for a house of at least 25 sq m.

s: Which of the following is NOT a component of PMAY-U?
x: The PMAY-U components include in-situ slum redevelopment, credit-linked subsidy, affordable housing in partnership and beneficiary-led construction. Rural tap-water supply belongs to the Jal Jeevan Mission.

s: PMAY-U 2.0, introduced in 2024, targets construction of how many urban houses?
x: PMAY-U 2.0 targets 1 crore urban houses.

s: In which year was Rajiv Awas Yojana, aimed at a slum-free India, subsumed into PMAY-Urban?
x: Rajiv Awas Yojana was subsumed into PMAY-U in 2015.

s: By which year did PMAY-Urban originally set the target of 'Housing for All'?
x: PMAY-U (2015) originally aimed at Housing for All by 2022.

s: What is the minimum unit size of a house under PMAY-Gramin?
x: PMAY-G houses must be at least 25 sq m.

s:
Consider the following statements about PMAY-Gramin:
1. It was restructured from Indira Awaas Yojana.
2. It has been extended up to 2028-29.
3. Unit assistance is ₹1.30 lakh in the plains.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: PMAY-G came from Indira Awaas Yojana and runs to 2028-29; unit assistance is ₹1.20 lakh in plains and ₹1.30 lakh in hilly areas.

s: In which year was Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana-Gramin launched?
x: PMAY-G began in 2016, restructured from Indira Awaas Yojana; PMAY-Urban began in 2015.

s: In which year did the Indira Awaas Yojana, later restructured as PMAY-Gramin, begin?
x: Indira Awaas Yojana began in 1985, became independent in 1996 and was restructured as PMAY-G in 2016.

s: Which of the following schemes is wrongly matched with its objective?
o: Ujjwala – Life and disability cover for rural landless households
Aam Aadmi Bima Yojana – Life and disability cover for rural landless households
x: Ujjwala provides free LPG connections to BPL women; life and disability cover is the Aam Aadmi Bima Yojana.

s: What is the annual premium of Pradhan Mantri Jeevan Jyoti Bima Yojana (PMJJBY)?
x: PMJJBY costs ₹436 a year (raised from ₹330 from 1 June 2022); ₹20 is the PMSBY premium.

s: What does Pradhan Mantri Suraksha Bima Yojana (PMSBY) provide?
o: Life cover of ₹2 lakh for death from any cause
Health cover of ₹5 lakh per family
Accident cover of ₹2 lakh for death or full disability
x: PMSBY is an accident scheme: ₹2 lakh for death/full disability, ₹1 lakh for partial; PMJJBY gives life cover.

s: To whom does Aam Aadmi Bima Yojana (2007) give life and disability cover?
x: Aam Aadmi Bima Yojana covers rural landless households.

s: Where was Ujjwala Yojana, giving free LPG connections to BPL women, launched on 1 May 2016?
x: Ujjwala was launched at Ballia (UP); Ranchi was PM-JAY's launch site and Jhunjhunu POSHAN's.

s: Which of the following is a social security programme?
o: Pradhan Mantri Jeevan Jyoti Bima Yojana
x: PMJJBY gives life cover to the poor and is a social security (insurance) scheme; the others are infrastructure or industry programmes.

s: Which scheme is known by the theme 'One Nation-One Scheme' and gives crop insurance against natural disasters?
o: Pradhan Mantri Jeevan Jyoti Bima Yojana
x: PMFBY is the crop insurance scheme against natural disasters with the theme 'One Nation-One Scheme'.

s: Against which of the following does Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana give insurance?
o: Crop loss due to natural disasters
Fall in market prices of crops
x: PMFBY is a crop insurance scheme that covers crop loss from natural disasters.

s: What is the annual premium of Pradhan Mantri Suraksha Bima Yojana (PMSBY)?
x: PMSBY premium was raised from ₹12 to ₹20 a year; ₹436 is the PMJJBY premium.

s: What is the life cover under Pradhan Mantri Jeevan Jyoti Bima Yojana for death from any cause?
x: PMJJBY gives a life cover of ₹2 lakh for death from any cause at ₹436 a year.

s: Which destitute elderly persons get free foodgrain under Annapurna?
o: Eligible for IGNOAPS but are not drawing it
x: Annapurna provides 10 kg of free grain to destitute elderly persons eligible for IGNOAPS but not receiving that pension.

s: What is the monthly pension under Andhra Pradesh's NTR Bharosa scheme?
x: NTR Bharosa provides ₹4,000 per month; AP's Universal Health Policy gives ₹2.5 lakh free cover to all.

s: What is the central assistance under IGNWPS and IGNDPS for beneficiaries aged 80 years and above?
x: Both schemes give ₹300 for the lower age group and ₹500 for beneficiaries aged 80 or above.

s: For whom was the National Pension System first introduced from 1 January 2004?
o: Central Government employees, excluding the armed forces
Employees of public sector banks only
All citizens of India, including the armed forces
x: NPS was introduced from 1 January 2004 for Central Government employees, with the armed forces excluded.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the National Pension System (NPS)?
o: It is a defined-contribution pension system
Both Tier I and Tier II accounts are mandatory
An extra deduction of ₹50,000 is available under Section 80CCD(1B)
x: Tier I is mandatory but Tier II is voluntary.

s: Under the Unified Pension Scheme (2025), what assured pension does an employee get after 25 years of service?
o: 40% of the last 12 months’ average basic pay
75% of the last 12 months’ average basic pay
50% of the last 12 months’ average basic pay
25% of the last month’s basic pay
x: UPS provides 50 per cent of the average basic pay of the last 12 months after 25 years of service. The minimum assured pension is ₹10,000.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Atal Pension Yojana (APY)?
o: Its eligible entry age is 18 to 60 years
Government support for it has been extended up to FY 2030–31
x: The eligible entry age for APY is 18 to 40 years.

s: Under PM-SYM, PM-KMY and NPS-Traders, what family pension is paid to the spouse?
x: The spouse receives 50 per cent of the pension as family pension under PM-SYM, PM-KMY and NPS-Traders.

s: For whom is the Pradhan Mantri Kisan Maandhan Yojana (PM-KMY) pension scheme meant?
o: Traders with turnover up to ₹1.5 crore
Unorganised workers earning up to ₹15,000 a month
Unorganised workers with a bank account
x: PM-KMY is for small and marginal farmers; traders are covered by NPS-Traders and low-wage unorganised workers by PM-SYM.

s: NSAP gives effect to which Directive Principle of State Policy?
x: NSAP gives effect to Article 41 of the Directive Principles, relating to public assistance in cases including old age, sickness and disablement.

s: Under the NSAP, the National Family Benefit Scheme gives assistance on the death of a breadwinner of which age group?
x: NFBS assists the family on the death of a breadwinner aged 18–59; 40–79 is the IGNWPS age band.

s: In which year was the National Social Assistance Programme (NSAP), which gives effect to Article 41, launched?
x: NSAP was launched in 1995 under the Ministry of Rural Development. 1985 is when Indira Awaas Yojana began, 2000 is AAY and Annapurna, and 2005 is JSY/MGNREGA.

s: Up to what monthly earning are unorganised workers covered under PM-SYM?
x: PM-SYM's income limit is Rs 15,000 a month; the Centre makes a 1:1 matching contribution.

s: Which one of the following statements about the National Pension System (NPS) is NOT correct?
o: It is a defined-contribution system regulated by PFRDA.
An NPS account can be opened and operated on behalf of a third person.
Tier I is mandatory while Tier II is voluntary.
x: An NPS account cannot be opened or operated for a third person (G2-GS 2024 key), so C is the incorrect statement. NPS is defined-contribution under PFRDA, OCIs may join, and Tier I is mandatory while Tier II is voluntary, so A, B and D are correct.

s: Who is the regulator of the National Pension System?
x: NPS is regulated by PFRDA, set up under an Act passed in 2013 and notified in 2014.

s: What is the range of the monthly pension at 60 under the Atal Pension Yojana?
x: APY gives ₹1,000-5,000 a month from own contribution; PM-SYM, PM-KMY and NPS-Traders give ₹3,000.

s: Under the NSAP, IGNDPS covers persons aged 18-79 with what minimum level of disability?
x: IGNDPS covers persons with disability of 80% or more.

s: What lump sum does the National Family Benefit Scheme pay?
x: NFBS pays ₹20,000 on the death of a breadwinner aged 18-59.

s: Which of the following pairs (Scheme – Monthly pension) is wrongly matched?
x: NPS-Traders, like PM-SYM and PM-KMY, gives ₹3,000 a month at 60.

s: What is the entry age for the Atal Pension Yojana?
x: APY entry age is 18-40; 16-59 is the e-Shram age band.

s: The Mukhyamantri Vishwakarma Pension Yojana for workers, street vendors and folk artists at 60 belongs to which State?
x: The Mukhyamantri Vishwakarma Pension Yojana is a Rajasthan scheme for workers, street vendors and folk artists aged 60.

s: Which State runs the NTR Bharosa pension for weavers, fishermen, toddy tappers and artisans?
x: NTR Bharosa is Andhra Pradesh's pension, ₹4,000 a month, for weavers, fishermen, toddy tappers, artisans and others.

s: For whom is NPS Vatsalya, launched in 2025, meant?
x: NPS Vatsalya (2025) is a pension account for minors, with a minimum contribution of ₹250.

s: In which year was the PFRDA Act, which made PFRDA the statutory regulator of the National Pension System, passed?
x: The PFRDA Act was passed on 19 September 2013 and notified on 1 February 2014.

s: Traders up to what annual turnover can join the NPS-Traders pension scheme?
x: NPS-Traders (2019) covers traders with turnover up to ₹1.5 crore and pays ₹3,000 a month at 60.

s: In which year was the National Pension System, introduced for government staff in 2004, opened to all citizens?
x: The NPS was introduced for government staff in 2004 and extended to all citizens in 2009.

s: Which of the following schemes were launched on 9 May 2015?
x: Pradhan Mantri Suraksha Bima Yojana, Pradhan Mantri Jeevan Jyoti Bima Yojana and Atal Pension Yojana were launched on 9 May 2015.

s: Which of the following schemes was launched earliest?
x: Aam Aadmi Bima Yojana dates from 2007; APY and PMSBY from 9 May 2015 and PM-JAY from September 2018.

s:
Arrange the following in chronological order of launch:
1. PM-JAY
2. Aam Aadmi Bima Yojana
3. Atal Pension Yojana
4. e-Shram
x: Aam Aadmi Bima Yojana (2007), APY (2015), PM-JAY (2018), e-Shram (2021).

s: What do Ayushman Arogya Mandirs, about 1.5 lakh upgraded Health and Wellness Centres, provide?
x: Ayushman Arogya Mandir aims to provide comprehensive primary care through about 1.5 lakh upgraded Health and Wellness Centres.

s: In which year did WHO certify India as polio-free?
x: India was certified polio-free in 2014; Pulse Polio began in 1995.

s: In which State is Shahdol, where the Sickle Cell Anaemia Elimination Mission was launched in July 2023?
x: Shahdol is in Madhya Pradesh; the mission aims to eliminate sickle cell anaemia by 2047.

s: For which purpose does Janani Suraksha Yojana, under the National Health Mission, give cash assistance?
x: JSY gives cash assistance for institutional delivery under the NHM and is 100 per cent centrally sponsored.

s: What are the two sub-missions of the National Health Mission?
x: NHM has two parts, the National Rural Health Mission and the National Urban Health Mission, with ASHAs and ANMs as its backbone.

s: What is the outlay of PM-ABHIM, which funds critical-care blocks and Integrated Public Health Labs?
x: PM-ABHIM (2021) has an outlay of ₹64,180 crore over 6 years for critical-care blocks, public health labs and pandemic preparedness.

s: In which year was Janani Suraksha Yojana launched under the National Health Mission?
x: JSY was launched in 2005 under NHM and is 100% centrally sponsored.

s: By which year does the Sickle Cell Anaemia Elimination Mission aim to eliminate sickle cell anaemia?
x: The mission, launched at Shahdol in July 2023, targets elimination by 2047.

s: Which programme was launched in December 2014 for full immunisation of children and pregnant women under the Universal Immunisation Programme?
x: Mission Indradhanush (Dec 2014) is a catch-up drive under the Universal Immunisation Programme for full immunisation of children and pregnant women.

s: In which year did the Pulse Polio programme begin in India?
x: Pulse Polio began in 1995; WHO certified India polio-free in 2014.

s: Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY provides health cover of how much per family per year for secondary and tertiary hospitalisation?
x: PM-JAY provides ₹5 lakh per family per year for secondary and tertiary hospitalisation.

s: In which areas does Ayushman Bharat target poor and vulnerable populations?
x: Ayushman Bharat targets poor and vulnerable populations in both rural and urban areas.

s: What is the general Centre-State funding ratio of PM-JAY?
x: PM-JAY is a Centrally Sponsored Scheme funded 60:40, rising to 90:10 for North-Eastern and Himalayan States.

s: On what basis is the eligibility of households under PM-JAY mainly decided?
x: PM-JAY uses SECC 2011 deprivation criteria, comprising six rural and eleven urban occupational criteria.

s: PM-JAY originally targeted what share of households at the bottom, about 10.74 crore families?
x: PM-JAY targets the bottom 40 per cent of households, about 10.74 crore poor and deprived families.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the senior citizen expansion of PM-JAY?
o: It is known as Ayushman Vay Vandana
It is limited to senior citizens aged 70 or above who are below the poverty line
A family already covered gets a ₹5 lakh top-up for the eligible senior citizen
x: Every person aged 70 or above is eligible irrespective of income.

s: Where was Ayushman Bharat–PM-JAY launched in September 2018?
x: PM-JAY, earlier called the National Health Protection Scheme, was launched at Ranchi in September 2018 and subsumed RSBY (2008).

s: How many SECC 2011 deprivation criteria are used for eligibility under PM-JAY?
x: PM-JAY uses 6 rural deprivation and 11 urban occupational criteria from SECC 2011.

s: Which earlier scheme was subsumed in Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY?
x: PM-JAY subsumed RSBY (2008); it was earlier called the National Health Protection Scheme.

s: Under which name does Andhra Pradesh's state health scheme, converged with PM-JAY, now run?
x: AP's scheme, begun as Rajiv Aarogyasri in 2007, now runs as Dr NTR Vaidya Seva converged with PM-JAY.

s: What was the earlier name of Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY?
x: PM-JAY was first called the National Health Protection Scheme; it subsumed RSBY (2008).

s:
Consider the following statements about Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY:
1. It is the world's largest health assurance scheme fully financed by the government.
2. It gives a cover of ₹5 lakh per family per year for secondary and tertiary hospitalisation.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: PM-JAY is the world's largest (not second-largest) government-funded health assurance scheme, with ₹5 lakh cover per family per year.

s: What is the Centre-State funding ratio of PM-JAY for North-Eastern and Himalayan States?
x: PM-JAY is funded 60:40 in general and 90:10 in North-Eastern and Himalayan States.

s: What is the Ayushman Bharat Health Account (ABHA)?
o: A registry of verified medical practitioners
A portal to track TB patients
A unique health ID that links a person's health records
x: ABHA is the unique health ID under ABDM linking a person's health records.

s: Ni-kshay is a case-based web portal for tracking patients of which disease?
x: Ni-kshay tracks TB patients; CoWIN handled COVID-19 vaccination.

s: U-WIN, modelled on CoWIN, is an electronic registry of what?
o: Routine immunisation of pregnant women and children
x: U-WIN records routine immunisation of pregnant women and children under UIP; CoWIN was for COVID-19 vaccines.

s: In which State was eSanjeevani, India's national telemedicine service, first rolled out?
x: eSanjeevani (2019) was first rolled out in Andhra Pradesh.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission:
1. It was launched in September 2021.
2. Its Healthcare Professionals Registry covers only modern medicine practitioners.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: ABDM launched in September 2021; the HPR covers practitioners of both modern and traditional systems, so 2 is wrong.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: U-WIN – Routine immunisation of pregnant women and children
x: U-WIN records routine immunisation; CoWIN was for COVID-19 vaccines, Ni-kshay tracks TB and eSanjeevani is telemedicine.

s: Which of the following is India's national telemedicine service?
x: eSanjeevani (2019) is the national telemedicine service; CoWIN and U-WIN are vaccination registries and Ni-kshay tracks TB.

s: Which body implements Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY at the national level?
x: PM-JAY is run by the National Health Authority (NHA); the Ministry of Jal Shakti runs the Jal Jeevan Mission.

s: Which one of the following correctly represents the benefits associated with EPFO coverage?
o: Unemployment allowance, family benefit and NFSA entitlement
Medical, maternity and dependants' benefits only
Provident fund, EPS pension and EDLI insurance
Old-age pension, maternity benefit and food subsidy only
x: The principal EPFO-linked benefits are provident fund accumulation, pension under the Employees' Pension Scheme and insurance under EDLI. Medical and maternity benefits are associated with ESI or other social-security provisions.

s: The Employees' Provident Fund generally covers establishments employing how many or more persons?
x: EPF generally covers establishments with 20 or more employees, with 12% of wages contributed each by employee and employer.

s: Which of the following is NOT a feature associated with the EPF Scheme, 2026?
o: Voluntary contributions above the prescribed ceiling
Exclusion of Aadhaar, PAN and UAN linkage requirements
Liability of the principal employer for contract workers' provident fund
x: Linking Aadhaar, PAN and UAN is mandatory under the EPF Scheme, 2026. The other three are stated features of the Scheme.

s: To what amount was the wage ceiling for mandatory EPFO coverage raised from ₹15,000?
x: The mandatory EPFO wage ceiling was raised from ₹15,000 to ₹25,000 per month. The earlier ₹15,000 ceiling had been in force since September 2014.

s: Under the ESI scheme, what are the employer's and employee's contributions respectively?
x: The employer contributes 3.25% and the employee 0.75%, with a wage ceiling of ₹21,000 per month.

s: The Code on Social Security, 2020 merged how many labour and social-security laws?
x: The Code on Social Security, 2020 merged nine laws, including laws relating to EPF, ESI, maternity benefit, gratuity and unorganised workers' social security.

s: Which body recommends social-security schemes for gig and platform workers under the Code on Social Security framework?
x: The National Social Security Board recommends social-security schemes for gig and platform workers under the framework.

s: Under the Code on Social Security, a creche is required in establishments with how many or more employees?
x: A creche is required at 50 or more employees; 20 is the EPF coverage threshold.

s: Which Ministry launched e-Shram, the National Database of Unorganised Workers, on 26 August 2021?
x: e-Shram was launched by the Ministry of Labour and Employment and gives a 12-digit UAN; income-tax payers and EPFO/ESIC members are excluded.

s: On which date did all four Labour Codes come into force?
x: All four Labour Codes, including the Code on Social Security, came into force on 21 November 2025, with Central Rules following in 2026. 17 April 2026 and 8 May 2026 are not the commencement date, and 2019 predates the 2020 Code.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Code on Social Security, 2020?
o: It is the first law to recognise aggregators, gig workers and platform workers
There is no cap on the aggregators' contribution
Aggregators must contribute 1–2 per cent of annual turnover to a social-security fund
The contribution is linked to the payments made to workers
x: The aggregator contribution is capped at 5 per cent of the payments made to workers.

s: What is the employee's contribution to EPF generally?
x: EPF contributions are 12% each from employer and employee (10% in notified establishments).

s: Under the Code on Social Security, aggregators contribute 1-2% of turnover, capped at what share of payouts?
x: Aggregators pay 1-2% of turnover, capped at 5% of payouts to gig and platform workers.

s: Which of the following is excluded from registering on e-Shram?
x: e-Shram excludes income-tax payers and EPFO/ESIC members; it covers unorganised workers aged 16-59.

s: How much maternity leave is given under the Code on Social Security, 2020?
x: The Code provides 26 weeks of maternity leave.

s:
Consider the following statements about the ESI scheme:
1. The wage ceiling is ₹21,000 a month.
2. It provides PF, EPS pension and EDLI insurance.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: ESI's ceiling is ₹21,000 and it gives medical, sickness and maternity benefits; PF, EPS and EDLI are EPFO benefits.

s: In which year was the Employees' State Insurance Act passed?
x: The ESI Act was passed in 1948.

s: Which of the following benefits is provided under the Employees' State Insurance (ESI) scheme?
x: ESI gives medical, sickness, maternity, disablement and dependants' benefits; PF, EPS and EDLI come under EPF.

s: What is the age limit for registration on the e-Shram portal?
x: Unorganised workers aged 16-59 can register on e-Shram and get a 12-digit UAN.

s: In which year was the e-Shram portal launched?
x: e-Shram was launched on 26 August 2021; 2019 is the year of PM-SYM, PM-KMY and NPS-Traders.

s: The principal target of Swachh Bharat Mission-Gramin Phase II is to create which of the following?
o: Functional tap connections in every urban household
x: SBM-Gramin Phase II focuses on ODF Plus villages. Garbage-free cities are the principal target of SBM-Urban 2.0.

s: On which of the following does Mission Poshan 2.0 mainly focus?
x: Mission Poshan 2.0 focuses on diet diversity, fortification and millets. It is implemented by the Ministry of Women and Child Development during 2021-22 to 2025-26.

s: Where was POSHAN Abhiyaan (National Nutrition Mission) launched on 8 March 2018?
x: POSHAN Abhiyaan was launched on 8 March 2018 at Jhunjhunu, Rajasthan. Shahdol is where the Sickle Cell Anaemia Elimination Mission was launched; Ranchi is where PM-JAY was launched; Panipat is a distractor.

s: NAMASTE is jointly associated with which two Ministries?
o: Ministry of Jal Shakti and Ministry of Education
Ministry of Health and Family Welfare and Ministry of Rural Development
Ministry of Labour and Employment and Ministry of Finance
Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment and Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs
x: NAMASTE is associated with the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment and the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs.

s: Under which Ministry is the Jal Jeevan Mission (2019), which aims at a tap connection for every rural home?
x: The Jal Jeevan Mission was launched in 2019 under the Ministry of Jal Shakti; Village Water and Sanitation Committees plan and run the supply.

s: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
o: Beti Bachao Beti Padhao promotes girl-child education.
Poshan Maah and Poshan Pakhwada are conducted annually in June and December.
Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan targets youth and educational institutions.
Accessible India Campaign seeks barrier-free physical and digital access.
x: Option B is incorrect: Poshan Maah and Poshan Pakhwada are bi-annual and held in September and March, not June and December.

s: Which Ministry is the lead ministry for Poshan Maah and Poshan Pakhwada?
x: The Poshan campaigns run at village and Anganwadi level under the Ministry of Women and Child Development.

s: POSHAN Abhiyaan brings together ICDS, the National Health Mission and which other mission?
x: POSHAN Abhiyaan converges ICDS, NHM and Swachh Bharat to tackle stunting, under-nutrition, anaemia and low birth weight.

s: Who set up the India Sanitation Coalition in June 2015 to support Swachh Bharat?
x: The India Sanitation Coalition was launched by FICCI on 25 June 2015.

s: On which date was the Swachh Bharat Mission launched?
x: SBM was launched on 2 October 2014 with the target of a clean India by 2 October 2019.

s: Under the Jal Jeevan Mission, who plans and runs village water supply?
x: Village Water and Sanitation Committees plan and run supply under the Jal Jeevan Mission.

s: Which of the following pairs (Programme – Nodal ministry) is wrongly matched?
o: POSHAN Abhiyaan – Women and Child Development
x: e-Shram is under the Ministry of Labour and Employment; the other pairs are correct.

s: In which months are Rashtriya Poshan Maah and Poshan Pakhwada held respectively?
x: Poshan Maah is held in September and Poshan Pakhwada in March - bi-annual drives, not June/December.

s: What is the objective of the NAMASTE scheme?
o: Free LPG connections to poor women
Ending hazardous manual cleaning of sewers and septic tanks
Piped water to every urban home
x: NAMASTE aims to end hazardous manual cleaning of sewers and septic tanks; it is run by MoSJE and MoHUA.

s: According to the Economic Survey 2016-17, lack of toilets makes women do which of the following?
x: The Economic Survey 2016-17 noted that lack of toilets makes women reduce their water intake.

s: Which of the following is wrongly matched?
o: Beti Bachao Beti Padhao – Awareness and enforcement against female foeticide
Accessible India Campaign – Auditing and retrofitting of public spaces
Poshan Maah & Poshan Pakhwada – Auditing and retrofitting of public spaces
Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan – Community mobilisation in high-vulnerability districts
x: Poshan Maah and Poshan Pakhwada are bi-annual mass nutrition sensitisation drives; auditing and retrofitting public spaces is the Accessible India Campaign.

s: In which villages does the Vibrant Villages Programme give reverse-migration incentives?
x: The Vibrant Villages Programme is a grassroots development campaign offering reverse-migration incentives in northern border villages.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Beti Bachao Beti Padhao – Border areas
Accessible India Campaign – Persons with Disabilities
Vibrant Villages Programme – Youth substance abuse
Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan – Women and child
x: Accessible India targets persons with disabilities; BBBP is about women and children, Vibrant Villages about border areas and Nasha Mukt Bharat about youth substance abuse.

s: Which Ministry implements the Vibrant Villages Programme?
x: Vibrant Villages is run by the Home Ministry; Nasha Mukt Bharat is under Social Justice and Poshan campaigns under Women and Child Development.

s:
Assertion (A): The SEED scheme provides PM-JAY coverage and PMAY housing support to Denotified, Nomadic and Semi-Nomadic Tribes.
Reason (R): SEED is administered by the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
x: Both are true: SEED is a Central Sector scheme of the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment that includes PM-JAY and PMAY support, but the ministry running it does not explain what it provides.

s: SEED, the scheme for Denotified, Nomadic and Semi-Nomadic Tribes, is a Central Sector scheme of which Ministry?
o: Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment
x: SEED (2022) is a Central Sector scheme of MoSJE with ₹200 crore over 5 years.

s: Which Ministries jointly run Beti Bachao Beti Padhao?
o: Women and Child Development, Health and Family Welfare, and Education
Social Justice, Rural Development, and Home Affairs
Women and Child Development, Labour, and Finance
Health and Family Welfare, Jal Shakti, and Education
x: Beti Bachao Beti Padhao is a joint campaign of MoWCD, MoHFW and the Ministry of Education.

s: Which of the following is a social assistance programme rather than a social insurance programme?
x: NSAP is non-contributory and tax-funded, so it is social assistance; EPF, APY and ESI are contributory social insurance.

s: How does social assistance differ from social insurance?
x: Social assistance is non-contributory, tax-funded and means-tested, while social insurance is contributory and tied to employment and risks.

s: ILO Convention No. 102, the Social Security (Minimum Standards) Convention, 1952, sets minimum standards for how many branches of social security?
x: Convention No. 102 covers nine branches of social security; India has not ratified it.

s: Which of the following is an example of social insurance rather than social assistance?
x: Social insurance is contributory and tied to employment (EPF, ESI, APY, PM-SYM); NSAP, NFSA and PM-JAY are tax-funded social assistance.

s:
Consider the following statements about ILO Convention No. 102:
1. It was adopted in 1952.
2. India has ratified it.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: C102, the Social Security (Minimum Standards) Convention, dates from 1952; India has not ratified it.

s: For how long are free NFSA foodgrains now provided under PMGKAY, which began during COVID-19 in 2020?
x: PMGKAY now provides free NFSA grains for 5 years from 1 January 2024. The other durations and start dates are not correct.

s:
Arrange the following phases of the Public Distribution System in chronological order:
A. Targeted Public Distribution System
B. Revamped Public Distribution System
C. Wartime rationing
D. Introduction of FCI and Agricultural Prices Commission
x: The correct sequence is wartime rationing in the 1940s, FCI and Agricultural Prices Commission in 1965, RPDS in June 1992, and TPDS in June 1997.

s: The Revamped Public Distribution System of June 1992 was the first to target which areas?
o: Urban households above the poverty line
x: RPDS, introduced in June 1992, was the first PDS reform to target hilly, tribal and remote areas.

s: Which were the 'two special schemes of 2000' meant for the poorest households and the destitute elderly?
o: PMGKAY and One Nation One Ration Card
x: The two special schemes of 2000 for target groups are Antyodaya Anna Yojana (poorest of the poor, 35 kg per household) and Annapurna (10 kg free grain for destitute elderly eligible for IGNOAPS but not drawing it). RPDS (1992) and TPDS (1997) are PDS phases; PMGKAY (2020) and ONORC (2019) are later; Mid-Day Meal is not one of the pair.

s: In which year was the Targeted Public Distribution System (TPDS) introduced?
x: TPDS dates from 1997 (the 'since when' PYQ). 1992 is the Revamped PDS, 2000 is AAY and Annapurna, and 2013 is the NFSA.

s: How much foodgrain does Antyodaya Anna Yojana, meant for the poorest of the poor, provide?
x: AAY gives 35 kg per household per month, not per person.

s: How much foodgrain per person per month do priority households get under the National Food Security Act?
x: Priority households get 5 kg per person per month; AAY households get 35 kg per household, and the maternity benefit is Rs 6,000.

s: In which year did the national rollout of One Nation One Ration Card begin?
x: ONORC's national rollout began in 2019.

s: How many people are covered under the National Food Security Act?
x: NFSA covers 79.8 crore people; 81.35 crore is the free-grain figure of August 2026.

s: How much free foodgrain does Annapurna give to destitute elderly persons?
x: Annapurna gives 10 kg of free grain a month; 35 kg per household is the AAY entitlement.

s: What is the maternity benefit under the National Food Security Act?
x: NFSA provides a maternity benefit of ₹6,000; ₹20,000 is the NFBS lump sum.

s: In which year was the Food Corporation of India set up along with the Agricultural Prices Commission?
x: FCI and the Agricultural Prices Commission came in 1965 to manage food deficits.

s: Which of the following is NOT a part of the FAO definition of food security?
o: Physical access to sufficient food for all
Economic access to food for all
x: FAO defines food security as physical and economic access for all to sufficient, safe, nutritious food; 'food of one's choice' is not part of it.

s: Saansad Adarsh Gram Yojana (SAGY) is a scheme of which Ministry?
x: SAGY is under the Ministry of Rural Development; it was launched on 11 October 2014, Jayaprakash Narayan's birth anniversary.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about MPLADS?
o: It is administered by the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation
Its unspent funds lapse at the end of each financial year
MPs recommend works, while the district authority executes them
It earmarks 15 per cent for SC areas and 7.5 per cent for ST areas
x: MPLADS funds are non-lapsable.

s: Which Ministry administers MPLADS?
o: Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation
x: MPLADS (1993) is under MoSPI; its funds are non-lapsable.

s: Under MPLADS, what are the earmarks for SC and ST areas respectively?
x: MPLADS earmarks 15% for SC and 7.5% for ST areas.

s: On which date was the Saansad Adarsh Gram Yojana (SAGY) launched?
x: SAGY was launched on 11 October 2014, the birth anniversary of Lok Nayak Jayaprakash Narayan.

s: Under the Saansad Adarsh Gram Yojana, who selects villages to be developed as model villages?
x: Under SAGY, MPs pick villages and develop them as model villages using existing programmes.

s: In which year was the Members of Parliament Local Area Development Scheme (MPLADS) launched?
x: MPLADS began in 1993; it is administered by MoSPI.

s: The PM-DevINE Portal is concerned primarily with which area?
o: Priority infrastructure and social impact projects in the North Eastern states
x: PM-DevINE funds and monitors priority infrastructure and social projects in all eight North-Eastern states.

s: Which organisation supports SANKALP, the MSDE programme to strengthen district-level skilling?
x: SANKALP is a World Bank-supported MSDE programme for district-level skilling institutions.

s: In which year was PMKVY 1.0, the flagship of the Skill India Mission, launched?
x: PMKVY 1.0 was launched in 2015 along with the Skill India Mission, not in 2016.

s: Which portal offers collateral-free and guarantor-free education loan applications with direct digital sanction?
x: The PM-Vidyalaxmi portal takes education-loan applications without collateral or guarantor, with digital sanction.

s: Which platform offers AI-aligned vocational certifications, apprenticeship matchmaking and PMKVY enrolment?
x: The Skill India Digital Hub offers AI-aligned certificates, apprenticeship matching and PMKVY enrolment.

s: Which of the following portals is wrongly matched with its ministry?
o: Skill India Digital Hub – Education (Higher Education)
National Cybercrime Reporting Portal – Home Affairs (I4C)
PM-DevINE Portal – Development of North Eastern Region
x: The Skill India Digital Hub comes under the Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship.

s: The MY Bharat portal comes under which Ministry?
o: Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship
Ministry of Development of North Eastern Region
Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports
x: The MY Bharat portal is under the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports.

s: Which is the nodal ministry for PMKVY?
o: Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship
x: PMKVY, the Skill India flagship, is under MSDE.

s: In June 2023, the Directorate General of Training (MSDE) signed an MoU with which company to train about 6,000 students in cybersecurity?
x: In June 2023 Microsoft and DGT (MSDE) signed an MoU to train about 6,000 students in cybersecurity.

s: In which year was NRLM renamed Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana-NRLM?
x: NRLM was restructured from SGSY in 2011 and renamed DAY-NRLM in 2016.

s: In which year was the National Rural Livelihoods Mission (NRLM), restructured from SGSY, launched?
x: NRLM was launched in 2011 by restructuring SGSY; it was renamed DAY-NRLM in 2016.

s: Under DAY-NRLM, what is the Centre-State funding ratio for North-Eastern States including Sikkim?
x: DAY-NRLM is funded 60:40 generally and 90:10 for NE States including Sikkim; UTs get 100% Central funding.

s: Which Ministry of Rural Development skilling programme is placement-linked for rural youth?
x: DDU-GKY is placement-linked for rural youth, while RSETIs focus on self-employment.

s: For what do RSETIs under the Ministry of Rural Development give training?
x: RSETIs give self-employment training; DDU-GKY is placement-linked skilling.

s: The target under the Lakhpati Didi initiative is to enable how many women to earn more than ₹1 lakh a year?
x: The Lakhpati Didi target is three crore women earning more than ₹1 lakh annually.

s: Under PMFBY, what is the farmer premium for commercial and horticultural crops?
x: The premium is 5% for commercial/horticultural crops, 2% for kharif and 1.5% for rabi.

s: In which year was PM-PRANAM, which aims to cut chemical fertiliser use, launched?
x: PM-PRANAM was launched in 2023; States share the subsidy saved.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: PMKSY — Har Khet Ko Pani and Per Drop More Crop
e-NAM — Pension for small and marginal farmers
x: PMKSY focuses on ‘Har Khet Ko Pani’ and ‘Per Drop More Crop’. Community groundwater management belongs to Atal Bhujal Yojana, pension to PM Kisan Maandhan and crop insurance to PMFBY.

s: At what age does a farmer under the PM Kisan Maandhan scheme start receiving the pension of ₹3,000 per month?
x: PM Kisan Maandhan is a contributory pension scheme providing ₹3,000 per month from the age of 60; entry is permitted between 18 and 40 years.

s: Where was the Soil Health Card scheme launched in 2015?
x: The Soil Health Card scheme was launched in 2015 at Suratgarh in Rajasthan.

s: Which agency assists Atal Bhujal Yojana, for community groundwater management in seven water-stressed States?
x: Atal Bhujal Yojana (Dec 2019) is World Bank-assisted; the World Bank also supports SANKALP.

s: What support does PM-KISAN give to landholding farmers?
x: PM-KISAN gives ₹6,000 a year in 3 instalments; ₹3,000 a month is the Maandhan pension.

s: Which is the lead agency for e-NAM, the online national agricultural market?
x: e-NAM (April 2016) links APMCs online, with SFAC as lead agency.

s: Under PMFBY, what is the farmer premium for kharif crops?
x: PMFBY premium is 2% for kharif, 1.5% for rabi and 5% for commercial/horticultural crops.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
x: PM-PRANAM (2023) aims to cut chemical fertiliser use; Soil Health Card was launched at Suratgarh, Maandhan pays ₹3,000 a month and e-NAM dates from 2016.

s: With which scheme are 'Har Khet Ko Pani' and 'Per Drop More Crop' associated?
x: PMKSY (2015) has the slogans 'Har Khet Ko Pani' and 'Per Drop More Crop'.

s: In which year was the Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (PMFBY) launched?
x: PMFBY was launched in 2016.

s: Which crop insurance schemes did the Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana replace?
x: PMFBY replaced the National Agricultural Insurance Scheme (NAIS) and Modified NAIS.

s: In which year was the National Agricultural Insurance Scheme (NAIS) introduced?
x: NAIS began in 1999-2000; PMFBY replaced it in 2016.

s: How is PM-KISAN, launched in February 2019, funded?
o: Centrally Sponsored Scheme with a 75:25 share
Centrally Sponsored Scheme with a 90:10 share
Centrally Sponsored Scheme with a 60:40 share
x: PM-KISAN is a 100% Central Sector scheme giving Rs 6,000 a year in three instalments.

s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
x: NREP was introduced in 1980, not 1983. RLEGP was introduced in 1983.

s: On which date did Swarnajayanti Gram Swarozgar Yojana (SGSY), which merged IRDP, TRYSEM and DWCRA, start?
x: SGSY started on 1 April 1999 by merging IRDP, TRYSEM, DWCRA and allied schemes (some keys, including APPSC 2025, give 1995). 1989 is JRY, 1993 is EAS, and 2011 is when NRLM was restructured from SGSY.

s: Jawahar Rozgar Yojana (1989) was formed by merging which programmes?
x: JRY (1989) merged NREP (1980) and RLEGP (1983). IRDP and TRYSEM went into SGSY (1999); EAS and JGSY formed SGRY (2001); DWCRA was also merged into SGSY.

s: Sampoorna Grameen Rozgar Yojana (SGRY, 2001) was formed by merging which schemes?
x: SGRY merged EAS and JGSY; JRY merged NREP and RLEGP.

s: Which of the following is NOT one of the six rural components of Bharat Nirman (2005)?
x: Bharat Nirman covered irrigation, roads, housing, drinking water, electrification and telephony - not skilling.

s: TRYSEM and DWCRA were sub-programmes of which programme?
x: TRYSEM and DWCRA were sub-programmes of IRDP, the Sixth Plan self-employment scheme.

s: In which year did the National Rural Employment Programme (NREP) begin?
x: NREP began in 1980, not 1983; RLEGP is 1983.

s: In which year was the Employment Assurance Scheme (EAS) launched?
x: EAS began in 1993; it was later merged with JGSY into SGRY in 2001.

s: VB-G RAM G, which replaces MGNREGA, guarantees how many days of work per household?
x: VB-G RAM G raises the guarantee to 125 days and is implemented through Panchayati Raj Institutions.

s: Under MGNREGA, at least what share of the workers had to be women?
x: MGNREGA required one-third of workers to be women; the Gram Sabha ran the social audit.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: VB-G RAM G – 100 days of work per household per year
MGNREGA – 100 days of unskilled manual work per household per year
VB-G RAM G – 75 days of skilled work per household per year
MGNREGA – 125 days of work per household per year
x: MGNREGA guaranteed 100 days of unskilled manual work per household per year; VB-G RAM G provides a 125-day guarantee.

s: On which date did the VB-G RAM G Act come into force?
x: It was introduced on 16 December 2025, got assent on 20 December 2025, was notified on 11 May 2026 and commenced on 1 July 2026.

s: What is the full form of VB-G RAM G?
o: Viksit Bharat—Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission (Gramin)
Viksit Bharat—Gram Rozgar and Awas Mission
Viksit Bharat—Gramin Rehabilitation and Manufacturing Mission
Village Bharat—Guarantee for Rural Agriculture and Migration
x: VB-G RAM G stands for Viksit Bharat-Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission (Gramin).

s: Under VB-G RAM G, who bears the unemployment allowance and delay compensation?
x: Under VB-G RAM G these are borne fully by the States; under MGNREGA the allowance was due if work was not given within 15 days.

s: Under MGNREGA, who conducted the social audit of works?
x: The Gram Sabha ran MGNREGA social audits; Gram Panchayats planned and carried out works.

s: Under MGNREGA, within how many days of demand did work have to be given to avoid unemployment allowance?
x: MGNREGA allowance was due if work was not given within 15 days, paid by States.

s: MGNREGA is linked to which Sustainable Development Goals?
x: MGNREGA links to SDG 1 (No Poverty) and SDG 8 (Decent Work).

s: What is the general Centre-State funding ratio under VB-G RAM G?
x: VB-G RAM G is a CSS with 60:40 funding (90:10 for NE/Himalayan States).

s:
Consider the following statements about MGNREGA:
1. One-third of the workers had to be women.
2. Works were planned and carried out by the Gram Panchayat.
3. It has been repealed by VB-G RAM G.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: All three are correct: one-third women, Gram Panchayat implementation, and repeal by VB-G RAM G.

s: Which State's SSAAT pioneered social audits of MGNREGA works?
x: Andhra Pradesh's Society for Social Audit, Accountability and Transparency (SSAAT) pioneered MGNREGA social audits under Section 17.

s: Under Geo-MGNREGA (2016), assets created are geotagged using which ISRO app?
x: Geo-MGNREGA geotags MGNREGA assets with ISRO's Bhuvan app.

s: What is the tagline of VB-G RAM G?
x: VB-G RAM G, which replaces MGNREGA with 125 days of work, has the tagline 'Rozgar Bhi, Samman Bhi'.

s: To whom does PM SVANidhi give working-capital loans starting at ₹10,000?
x: PM SVANidhi supports street vendors with a first loan of ₹10,000, a 7 per cent interest subsidy and digital cashback.

s: Andhra Pradesh's Amaravati is included under which of the following schemes?
x: On the AP side, Amaravati is a HRIDAY city. SPMRM develops Rurban clusters, SVAMITVA does drone surveys of village houses, and PM e-Bus Sewa provides city e-buses.

s: The Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs was formed in 2017 by merging which two ministries?
o: Housing and Urban Poverty Alleviation and Urban Development
Housing and Finance and Urban Development
Social Justice and Housing and Urban Affairs
x: MoHUA was formed in 2017 by merging the Ministry of Housing and Urban Poverty Alleviation with the Ministry of Urban Development.

s: In June 2023, DAY-NULM entered into a partnership with which organisation to empower women?
x: DAY-NULM partnered with UNDP in June 2023 to empower women (APPSC 2023). The World Bank backs Atal Bhujal and SANKALP; UN-Habitat and ADB are distractors.

s: Which programme aims at tap water to all households in statutory towns?
x: AMRUT 2.0 (2021) aims at tap water for all households in statutory towns; SBM-Urban 2.0 targets garbage-free cities.

s: How many cities are covered under the Smart Cities Mission?
x: The Smart Cities Mission covers 100 cities; HRIDAY covers 12.

s: How many e-buses does PM e-Bus Sewa (2023) aim to provide?
x: PM e-Bus Sewa provides 10,000 e-buses for city services on PPP.

s: Which of the following is one of the 12 HRIDAY heritage cities?
